Keywords: cluster autoscaling, instance pools, cold start, idle cluster
Guidance: Fixed-size clusters left running idle between jobs burn compute cost, while cold-starting a new cluster per job adds minutes of startup latency to every run.
Do: Use autoscaling clusters sized with min/max bounds, and instance pools to keep a warm buffer of ready VMs for frequently-started jobs.
Don't: Run a fixed-size always-on cluster sized for peak load when workload is bursty and infrequent.

Topic: Delta Lake ACID and time travel
Keywords: delta lake, acid transactions, time travel, versioned table
Guidance: Writing directly to Parquet without Delta Lake gives no transactional guarantees -- concurrent writers can corrupt a table, and there's no built-in way to query or roll back to a prior version.
Do: Use Delta Lake tables for anything with concurrent writers or a need for historical versioning/rollback via time travel.
Don't: Write concurrently to raw Parquet files with no transaction log, risking partial/corrupted reads.
Example: SELECT * FROM my_table VERSION AS OF 12;

Keywords: databricks workflows, job orchestration, notebook dependencies
Guidance: Manually running notebooks in sequence (or via ad-hoc external cron) has no dependency tracking, retry logic, or failure alerting built in.
Do: Use Databricks Workflows (Jobs) to define notebook/task dependencies, retries, and alerting as a proper DAG.
Don't: Chain notebook execution manually or through an unrelated external scheduler with no native dependency tracking.

Keywords: unity catalog, data governance, table acl, lineage
Guidance: Without Unity Catalog, table-level access control and column lineage are inconsistent across workspaces, making audits and least-privilege enforcement hard at scale.
Do: Adopt Unity Catalog for centralized access control, auditing, and lineage tracking across all workspaces.
Don't: Manage table permissions ad hoc per-workspace with legacy Hive metastore and no central governance layer.
Example: GRANT SELECT ON TABLE catalog.schema.table TO `analyst_group`;

Keywords: job cluster, all-purpose cluster, interactive cluster, cost
Guidance: Running scheduled production jobs on an all-purpose (interactive) cluster costs significantly more per DBU than a job cluster, which is billed at a lower rate and is ephemeral by design.
Do: Run scheduled/production jobs on job clusters (created and torn down per run); reserve all-purpose clusters for interactive development.
Don't: Schedule production ETL jobs against a shared, always-on all-purpose interactive cluster.

Guidance: The Spark default of 200 shuffle partitions is rarely right for both very small and very large datasets, causing either excessive task overhead or too-few partitions to parallelize effectively.
Do: Tune spark.sql.shuffle.partitions (or use Adaptive Query Execution) based on actual data volume rather than leaving the 200 default unexamined.
Don't: Leave shuffle partition count at the default 200 for both tiny and multi-terabyte datasets.

Keywords: dbfs, unity catalog volumes, file storage, deprecated storage
Guidance: DBFS root storage mixes data across workspaces with no fine-grained governance and is being phased out in favor of Unity Catalog Volumes for managing non-tabular files.
Do: Use Unity Catalog Volumes for new file storage needs instead of writing to the DBFS root.
Don't: Write new pipeline outputs directly to the DBFS root without a governance layer.

Keywords: optimize, z-order, small file problem, compaction
Guidance: Streaming or frequent-write pipelines create many small files over time (the 'small file problem'), degrading read performance until compaction is run.
Do: Run OPTIMIZE (with ZORDER BY on commonly-filtered columns) periodically on frequently-written Delta tables.
Don't: Let a high-write-frequency Delta table accumulate small files indefinitely with no OPTIMIZE schedule.

Keywords: photon engine, databricks runtime, ml runtime, vectorized engine
Guidance: Running on an older Databricks Runtime without Photon enabled leaves significant query performance (and therefore cost-per-query) on the table for SQL/DataFrame-heavy workloads.
Do: Enable Photon and keep clusters on a current LTS Databricks Runtime for SQL and DataFrame-heavy workloads.
Don't: Run production SQL-heavy workloads on an old runtime with Photon disabled by default.

Keywords: databricks secrets, secret scope, credential storage
Guidance: Hardcoding database passwords or API keys directly in notebook cells exposes them in notebook history, version control, and to anyone with notebook read access.
Do: Store credentials in a Databricks secret scope (backed by Azure Key Vault or Databricks-managed) and reference them via dbutils.secrets.get.
Don't: Hardcode API keys or passwords as plaintext strings in notebook cells.

Keywords: structured streaming, checkpoint location, exactly-once, watermark
Guidance: A streaming job with no (or a shared) checkpoint location can't resume correctly after a failure, risking reprocessing or data loss on restart.
Do: Give every Structured Streaming query its own dedicated, durable checkpoint location for exactly-once recovery semantics.
Don't: Share a single checkpoint location across multiple streaming queries, or omit it entirely.

Guidance: Repeatedly recomputing the same expensive DataFrame transformation across multiple downstream actions wastes cluster compute that a single .cache()/.persist() call would avoid.
Do: Cache/persist DataFrames that are reused across multiple actions, and unpersist when no longer needed to free executor memory.
Don't: Recompute the same expensive multi-stage transformation from scratch for every downstream action with no caching.
